concepts.name: Leadership versus management
concepts.summary: Explain how leadership (setting direction, influencing people) differs from and overlaps with management (planning, organising, controlling work).

concepts.name: Formal and informal leadership
concepts.summary: Distinguish leadership that comes from a position from leadership that comes from influence and recognise that both exist in teams.

concepts.name: Core leadership styles
concepts.summary: Name and describe the classic styles such as autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire.

concepts.name: Transformational, servant and situational leadership
concepts.summary: Recall the central idea of each of the three named theories in one sentence.

concepts.name: Purpose of a vision
concepts.summary: Explain that a vision describes a desired future that gives a team direction and meaning.

concepts.name: Trust as foundation
concepts.summary: Explain why followers need to trust a leader's competence, intentions and consistency before they willingly follow.

concepts.name: Leading by example
concepts.summary: Understand that a leader's observable behaviour sets the standard a team actually follows.

misconceptions.text: Leaders are born with charisma and leadership cannot be learned.
Leadership is the same thing as holding a senior job title.
A good leader is simply the one who gives the best orders.

concepts.name: Transformational leadership components
concepts.summary: Describe idealised influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation and individualised consideration and recognise each in behaviour.

concepts.name: Servant leadership principles
concepts.summary: Explain how putting followers' growth and needs first, through listening, empathy and stewardship, shapes a leader's actions.

concepts.name: Situational leadership matching
concepts.summary: Choose directing, coaching, supporting or delegating according to a person's competence and commitment on a given task.

concepts.name: Writing a clear vision
concepts.summary: Draft a concise, concrete and inspiring vision for a small team that links to its purpose and values.

concepts.name: Trust-building behaviours
concepts.summary: Use consistent behaviours such as keeping promises, being open and admitting mistakes to build trust with a team.

concepts.name: Power bases
concepts.summary: Identify legitimate, reward, coercive, expert and referent power and explain how each affects followers.

concepts.name: Basic influence methods
concepts.summary: Apply simple influence tactics such as rational persuasion, consultation and inspirational appeals to gain support without relying on authority.

misconceptions.text: Servant leadership means the leader is weak and does whatever followers ask.
Situational leadership means a leader should change their personality to suit each person.
A vision statement is just a slogan, and writing it is the whole job of creating a vision.

concepts.name: Diagnosing readiness for style choice
concepts.summary: Analyse a team member's skill and motivation per task and justify the leadership style adjustment that results.

concepts.name: Communicating vision across audiences
concepts.summary: Adapt and repeat a vision through stories, symbols and concrete goals so that different audiences understand why it matters to them.

concepts.name: Contingency and path-goal thinking
concepts.summary: Analyse how task structure, follower traits and context determine which leader behaviour is effective.

concepts.name: Leader-member exchange
concepts.summary: Analyse how differing relationship quality with individual followers creates in-groups and out-groups and affects fairness and performance.

concepts.name: Motivating through autonomy and purpose
concepts.summary: Design work, goals and recognition that build autonomy, mastery and purpose rather than relying only on rewards.

concepts.name: Trust repair after breaches
concepts.summary: Analyse the cause of a trust breach (competence versus integrity) and select actions to repair it.

concepts.name: Coaching conversations
concepts.summary: Run structured conversations that use questions and feedback to build another person's capability rather than giving answers.

misconceptions.text: A leader should treat everyone identically to be fair.
Announcing the vision once, clearly, is enough to get people to adopt it.
Trust broken by a leader is restored by a sincere apology alone.

concepts.name: Integrating leadership theories critically
concepts.summary: Evaluate the evidence and limits of transformational, servant and situational models and combine them to suit a context.

concepts.name: Leading change
concepts.summary: Judge and sequence actions to create urgency, build a coalition, anchor change and handle resistance.

concepts.name: Leader development pipelines
concepts.summary: Evaluate stretch assignments, mentoring and feedback systems for their ability to grow leaders at multiple levels.

concepts.name: Psychological safety and dissent
concepts.summary: Analyse how leader behaviour creates or erodes safety for candour, and assess its effect on learning and decisions.

concepts.name: Shaping organisational culture
concepts.summary: Analyse how artefacts, espoused values and underlying assumptions form a culture and how leader behaviour, rewards and rituals reinforce it.

concepts.name: Influence without authority
concepts.summary: Evaluate stakeholder interests and choose coalition and negotiation strategies to lead across teams where there is no formal power.

concepts.name: Ethical and values-based leadership
concepts.summary: Judge leadership decisions against ethical principles and the leader's stated values, including the risk of manipulative charisma.

misconceptions.text: A strong inspirational vision overcomes the need to manage resistance to change.
Culture is set by posters and value statements rather than by what leaders reward and tolerate.
Psychological safety means lowering standards and avoiding conflict.

concepts.name: Designing leadership systems
concepts.summary: Create structures, roles and decision rights that spread leadership across the organisation and reduce dependence on individuals.

concepts.name: Culture transformation strategy
concepts.summary: Design a multi-year plan that aligns incentives, rituals, hiring and leader behaviour to shift a culture and measure that it holds.

concepts.name: Evaluating leadership effectiveness
concepts.summary: Judge the validity of measures such as 360 feedback, engagement data and outcomes when assessing a leader or program.

concepts.name: Leading through crisis and ambiguity
concepts.summary: Evaluate decisions and communications under pressure, balancing speed, transparency and the maintenance of trust.

concepts.name: Building a leadership philosophy
concepts.summary: Synthesise theory, experience and values into a coherent, testable personal approach to leading that evolves with feedback.

concepts.name: Leadership across cultures and contexts
concepts.summary: Evaluate how national, industry and organisational cultures change which leadership behaviours are effective and adapt accordingly.

concepts.name: Leadership succession and legacy
concepts.summary: Create succession approaches that preserve purpose and culture while letting new leaders reshape direction.

misconceptions.text: A culture change succeeds once top leaders announce new values and a few role models adopt them.
Leadership effectiveness can be read directly from financial results or from popularity scores.
Best-practice leadership behaviours from one culture transfer unchanged to any other.
